heroHeadline: NYT Investigation Finds Fraud and Waste in Ukrainian Defense Procurement Unchecked as Implicated Contractors Win Further Weapons Contracts
heroSubtitle: Russia bombarded Kyiv and its suburbs for a sixth consecutive night into September 1 with ballistic missiles, Kalibr cruise missiles, and 218 drones, destroying a Ukrzaliznytsia railway depot workshop and killing 12 people including 6 rail workers, with a separate strike on Brovary killing 4 more. On September 2, Russian drones struck Kyiv's National University of Food Technology during classes and a residential building in Shevchenkivskyi district, injuring at least 13 on the seventh straight day of near-continuous attacks on the capital. Amid the barrages, President Zelensky warned foreign airlines and insurers that Russian airspace was no longer safe from Ukrainian long-range drone strikes; President Putin, speaking at the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation summit in Bishkek, called the warning 'a bid for state terrorism' and said Moscow would 'find a way to respond,' sending Aeroflot shares down over 5%. Russian cumulative personnel losses reached approximately 1,491,030 by September 2, per the Ukrainian General Staff.
footerNote: Data sourced from UN OHCHR, ISW, CSIS, Ukrainian MoD, US DoD, NATO, IAEA, EU Council, UK MoD, and major news outlets including Reuters, BBC, AP, Al Jazeera, CNN, Bloomberg, Kyiv Independent, Ukrinform, Ukrainska Pravda, Kyiv Post, Euronews, PBS NewsHour, GlobalSecurity.org, United24 Media, Wikipedia War Timeline, and the Ukrainian General Staff. Casualty figures are estimates; Russia has never released official figures.
